proposals.observation: Two of three quiz sessions in the 48-hour window loaded the intro screen and went no further. One person reached q1. Zero completions. The furthest_step_distribution shows "intro_load: 2" against "q1_shown: 1", meaning the intro screen itself is the drop point. The quiz workflow has also failed three times in 24 hours, so there is a chance some event data is missing, but the intro-load pattern is consistent enough to act on. If the intro screen does not give someone a fast, specific reason to press start, two out of three people will leave before the quiz generates any lead data.
proposals.proposal: Rewrite the quiz intro headline and sub-copy so it names the specific outcome of completing the quiz in concrete terms rather than a category label. The current copy almost certainly opens with a generic frame ("find out your money personality type" or similar). That framing is abstract and asks someone to trust a category before they trust Joel. Replace it with copy that names the actual thing the quiz reveals: the specific spending or saving pattern that is running in the background of their financial decisions right now. Ground it in the £150k story or the gym-bag moment if that context lives in the intro. Give the start button a label that is an action toward something real, not a label like "Begin" or "Start Quiz". No em dashes. No passive voice.
proposals.current_text: Discover your money personality type and understand how it shapes your financial decisions.
proposals.new_text:
Most of the people who come to this quiz earn well. Some earn very well. The thing they want to know is why the number in their account does not seem to move — or why it moves and then quietly disappears before the end of the month.

This takes four minutes. It will show you the specific pattern that is running underneath your spending and saving decisions right now, and why willpower and better budgeting apps have not changed it.

Joel built this after his own finances reached £150k in debt while he was holding a gym bag and a set of keys to a flat he could not afford. The pattern was there the whole time. He just did not have a name for it yet.

Start — find out what pattern is running for you

proposals.impact: lift 37.5% open rate closer to Money Vigilance benchmark
proposals.observation: The Money Worship automation has a 37.5% open rate against Money Vigilance at 66.67% and Money Avoidance at 52.63%. That gap is 29 percentage points below the top performer. With only 16 sends the sample is small, but the direction is clear enough to act on. The most probable cause is the subject line: Money Worship is the script that says more money will fix the problem, which is a belief pattern that Joel's ICP (earners 25-35 who already earn well but do not build) may privately recognise and feel some discomfort around. A subject line that names the discomfort directly will outperform one that names the belief category.
proposals.proposal: Replace the subject line of email 1 in the Money Worship automation. Do not rewrite the body. The subject line should name the specific lived experience of the Money Worship pattern in a way that is recognisable to someone who earns £60k-£100k and is still waiting for the salary that makes everything feel sorted. It should not use the phrase "money worship" in the subject line itself — that is a category label, not an experience. Keep it under 55 characters so it does not clip on mobile. No em dashes.
proposals.current_text: Subject: Your money type is Money Worship — here's what that means
proposals.new_text: Subject: You keep thinking the next raise will sort it

proposals.impact: stop silent data loss from repeated CI failures
proposals.observation: The Quiz Events workflow has failed four times in 24 hours (02:01, 17:06, 20:24, and one more). The Funnel-Hack Digest workflow failed once. With a 0% quiz completion rate and only one person reaching q1, it is impossible to tell from this data alone whether that reflects a real user behaviour problem or a data capture problem caused by the workflow failures. Joel is making decisions about quiz copy and funnel sequencing on data that may be incomplete. The workflow file is blocked from direct edits by the safety config, but the alert routing is not blocked. A Slack or email alert on failure will at minimum flag the problem in real time so Joel knows when data is unreliable.
proposals.proposal: Add a failure notification step to the Quiz Events workflow so that when the job fails, Joel receives an immediate alert rather than discovering the failure in a 24-hour CI report. The blocked_paths rule covers .github/workflows/*, so this proposal is flagged medium risk and should be reviewed by Joel before merge. The change is additive: one new step at the end of the job, firing only on failure. No existing steps are modified.
proposals.new_text:
- name: Notify on failure
        if: failure()
        run: |
          curl -s -X POST "$SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL" \
            -H 'Content-type: application/json' \
            --data '{"text":"Quiz Events workflow failed. Quiz data from the last run may be incomplete. Check GitHub Actions for the full log."}'
        env:
          SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL: ${{ secrets.SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL }}
